newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Lex car dealership sale to Pendragon.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Lex car dealership sale to Pendragon.

text.p: Lex Service Plc, one of Britain's biggest vehicle leasing groups, embarked on a strategic refocus on Friday by selling its low-margin volume car dealership network to Pendragon Plc for 44 million pounds ($73.5 million).
Pendragon clinched the deal as part of a wider 64 million pounds investment which will be partly funded by a four-for-seven rights issue to raise 56 million.

Lex, which also reported half year pretax and pre-exceptional profits of 30.4 million pounds, saw its shares accelerate by six pence to 406 1/2, but Pendragon shares went into reverse on the news, falling 26 pence to 322 1/2.

Lex chief executive Andy Harrison said in a statement the company had "made an important strategic move which will focus Lex Retail on fewer, specialist manufacturers where we have a good track record of performance".
"This is a core business which we intend to develop."
David Leibling, director of corporate communications at Lex, told Reuters the remaining dealership network would be expanded.
"We plan to invest up to 10 million pounds in development and (make) further acquisitions," he said.
Lex has jettisoned the volume end of the market with cars like Ford and Vauxhall and is concentrating on the value end of the market, including names like Mercedes and Jaguar.
Pendragon said in its statement its expansion included plans for a further 30 franchise points at a total investment of 64 million pounds.
To help strengthen its balance sheet for these developments, Pendragon said it was seeking to raise around 56 million pounds rights issue of just over 22 million shares at 265 pence a share.
"The acquisition from Lex and the new development significantly expand Pendragon's relationships within the volume sector of the market," said Pendragon's chief executive Trevor Finn.
"The move towards large franchise territories will result in significant economies of scale and we now have the financial resources to develop fully these new opportunities".
Lex will receive 40 percent of the sale proceeds on completion, seen at the end of September, 30 percent after one year and 30 percent after two years.
The sale gives a 10 percent discount off the book value of assets and is earnings neutral for Lex.
A six million pounds hit for associated costs plus 25 million in goodwill will also be charged to Lex.
Turning to Lex's results, published at the same time as the deal details, turnover fell back to 777.3 million pounds from 812.1 million, with the half year payout at 6.8 pence per share versus 6.4.

Lex vehicle leasing profit rose 17 percent, reflecting strong fleet car market growth. The Hyundai Car (UK) division saw car registrations up 46 percent and lifted UK market share to 1.1 percent and lift trucks saw profits up 14 percent. But Multipart, the automotive parts distributor, saw a fallback in profit due to buying a new computer system.
